issues.description: Dogfood section says '4 Evaluator verdicts (2 on Increment 0, 2 on Increment 1; none on Increment 2 yet)', but the review's own Evaluator section describes rounds 1 and 2 on incr2_review. `bash scripts/dogfood.sh report` now prints 'evaluator verdicts: pass 5', and telemetry.jsonl has a 5th event for incr2_review (score 7.4, 2026-10-02T14:18:31Z). The review's claim that rounds 1 and 2 both read 14:40:00Z cannot be matched to telemetry, which shows 14:18:31Z. The count is stale and internally inconsistent.

The disclosure that docs/07 and CONTRACT.md were changed ahead of approval says 'both revert (`git revert` of that commit)'. No such commit exists. `git status` shows CONTRACT.md, docs/07, docs/02, docs/04, docs/05, gates.yaml and the tests as uncommitted modifications. HEAD is the judge_retest gate commit. The disclosure of the early update is honest, but the described revert mechanism is wrong.

T9 findings say Sonnet 'finished fastest' and the Decision says 'the fastest'. The table bolds E's 541-682 s although arm A has a 530 s run (gen-glm-3). The review correctly qualifies this as mean wall time only (591 s against 694 s). docs/04 still carries the unqualified claim that the review corrected.

The Deviations list omits SPEC departures that matter. (a) SPEC's T7 measurement required arm (b), prompt-as-variable, built and run with 2 repeats per arm. It was not built. The decision rests on a ceiling argument. This is stated under Decisions and in the carry-overs, but not in 'Deviations and caveats' and not as a SPEC deviation. (b) SPEC says ideas default to 5 and a `loop.best_idea` Choice gate. The run used 3 ideas and no best-idea gate. (c) The review treats 'a perfect context technique saves at most 14-23% of the bill' as if it closed T2's reverse-if (2), although SPEC wanted a measured comparison.

The re-test section says '26 runs' gates.jsonl: 168 records'. The 168 `loop.*` records come from all 30 gates.jsonl files, as the review itself says in the idea_worth_run bullet. split.json's 'runs_used: 26' counts the runs that contributed kept items, not the source of the 168 records.

The review calls the roughly 795 s residual 'sandboxed TreeHFD time (three seeds on two datasets...)'. The reported TreeHFD runtime_s values in results.json sum to about 390 s: baseline about 95 s, C2 about 182 s, C3 about 109 s. The 795 s is 849 minus model latency, and includes container starts, xgboost fitting, the retry and orchestration. It is a residual, not a measured sandbox time.

AUD-P-02 records 'about 10 s' of audit wall time. docs/results/loop-001/audit_report.json records wall_seconds: 1, and the four Jev calls took 144-284 ms each. The review does not discuss AUD-P-02 at all. The 10 s figure has no support in the repo.

R10 reads '$0.052 per complete run with Sonnet 5.5, about $0.002 with GLM, about 110 times below the estimate'. The 110x ratio holds only for Sonnet (5.7/0.052 = 110). The GLM figure is a comparison run that excludes the baseline stage, measured against a $0.5 estimate (about 260x). The wording is ambiguous.

The seeded-fault caveat says the faults are 'mostly deterministic... a changed digit', so 100% says little about subtle ones. The test set includes small, near-miss perturbations such as 5.15 to 5.14 and 30.9 to 30.2 (manifest.csv). These were all detected, so the review understates what was exercised and does not say which fault was the only one that tested a configuration number. Also unmentioned: an untracked ContextLanguageModels.pdf in the repo root, which the carry-over list on tmp/ and other untracked files does not name.

notes: GAPS: 1) Stale/contradictory Evaluator count (4 and 'none on Increment 2' vs 5 in dogfood report, rounds 1-2 in the review, telemetry 14:18:31Z). 2) Revert instruction refers to a commit that does not exist (changes are uncommitted). 3) docs/04 T9 still says Sonnet is 'fastest' (GLM run 530 s was faster; only the mean is shortest). 4) Deviations list omits the unbuilt T7 arm (b), the 3-ideas-not-5 and missing best_idea gate, and presents the T7 ceiling as closing T2 reverse-if (2). 5) '26 runs' vs 30 gates.jsonl files wording. 6) 795 s labelled 'sandboxed TreeHFD time' is a residual; reported runtimes sum to about 390 s. 7) docs/02 AUD-P-02 '~10 s' vs recorded 1 s. 8) R10 wording ties 110x to GLM as well as Sonnet. 9) No human spot-check of audit findings and Jev-judged audit claims are disclosed, but there is no measured audit judge accuracy (acknowledged in the review). 10) Actual OpenRouter billing is not reconciled against ledgers (disclosed).
